Grammar Focus — Verb + -ing / Verb + to …
今日の文法のポイントを確認しましょう。
A動詞 ＋ -ing
動詞の後ろに別の動詞を続けるとき、-ing にするか to … にするかは前の動詞で決まります。次の動詞の後ろは -ing（to は使えません）。
enjoy / mind / finish /
avoid / suggest ＋ -ing
楽しむ／気にする（嫌がる）／終える／避ける／提案する。Would you mind -ing? ＝「～していただけますか」
Would you mind turning the music down?
（音楽の音量を下げていただけますか？）
give up / put off /
keep (on) ＋ -ing
give up ＝ やめる／put off ＝ 先延ばしにする／keep (on) ＝ ～し続ける・何度も～する
She kept talking during the movie.
（彼女は映画の間ずっとしゃべっていた。）
not ＋ -ing
否定は -ing の前に not を置く。
He suggested not going out because of the storm.
（嵐なので出かけないようにしようと彼は提案した。）
※ ×Would you mind to turn … → ○ Would you mind turning …　／　×He suggested to go. → ○ He suggested going.
B動詞 ＋ to …
次の動詞の後ろは to ＋ 動詞の原形。「これからすること」に向かう意味の動詞が多いのが特徴です。
decide / plan / hope /
promise / agree / refuse
＋ to …
決める／計画する／望む／約束する／同意する／断る
She refused to answer my question.
（彼女は私の質問に答えるのを拒んだ。）
manage / afford ＋ to …
manage ＝（苦労して）なんとか～できる／can't afford ＝（お金・時間の）余裕がない
Did you manage to get tickets?
（チケット、なんとか取れた？）
not to …
否定は to の前に not を置く。
He decided not to apply for the job.
（彼はその仕事に応募しないことにした。）
C動詞 ＋ 人 ＋ to …
「人に～してほしい・～するように頼む／言う」は、動詞の後ろに人を入れて to … を続けます。
THE STRUCTURE IS:
I want to go.（自分が行きたい）
↓ 人を入れる
I want you to go.（あなたに行ってほしい）
want / would like /
expect ＋ 人 ＋ to …
人に～してほしい／～すると思っている（期待する）。Do you want me to …? / Would you like me to …? ＝「～しましょうか？」
Would you like me to take a picture?
（写真、撮りましょうか？）
ask / tell / remind /
advise / allow
＋ 人 ＋ to …
頼む／言う（指示する）／思い出させる／勧める／許可する
The doctor told me to rest for a few days.
（医者に数日休むように言われた。）
※ want の後ろに that 節は使いません：×I want that you help me. → ○ I want you to help me.
Dmake / let ＋ 人 ＋ 動詞の原形（to なし）
make と let は、人の後ろに to を付けずに動詞の原形を続けます。
make ＋ 人 ＋ 動詞の原形
（無理に・強制的に）～させる
The teacher made us rewrite the essay.
（先生は私たちに作文を書き直させた。）
let ＋ 人 ＋ 動詞の原形
（許可して）～させてあげる。Let me … ＝「私に～させて」
My boss let me leave early today.
（今日は上司が早く帰らせてくれた。）
※ ×She made me to wait. → ○ She made me wait.
※ suggest は「人 ＋ to」の形をとりません：×She suggested me to see a doctor. → ○ She suggested seeing a doctor.

Listening 1 Vocabulary Note

JLPT
The Japanese-Language Proficiency Test. N5 is the easiest level and N1 is the hardest.
日本語能力試験
persuade someone to ~
To make someone agree to do something by giving them good reasons.
（人）を説得して～させる
I know the feeling.
I understand, because the same thing has happened to me.
その気持ち、よくわかる
give it a try
To try doing something to see if it works.
試しにやってみる
Deal!
Used to say "I agree" to an offer or promise.
決まり！、それで行こう！

Listening 2 Vocabulary Note
quiet zone
An area where people must not talk loudly or make noise.
静かに過ごすエリア、サイレントゾーン
phone booth
A small closed space where one person can make phone or video calls.
電話ブース、通話用の個室
regulars
Customers who come to the same place very often.
常連客
save a seat
To keep a seat for yourself or someone else, e.g. by putting a bag on it.
席を取っておく

Dialogue Practice — Ondoku
オーディオを聞いて、繰り返し音読練習をしましょう。ハイライト語句にカーソルを当てると日本語が表示されます。
DIALOGUE AUDIO
Aileen & Mai — Bridge
Aileen
Mai! How did the interview go? I've been dying to hear.
Mai
Honestly, better than I expected! Charlotte's practice interview really helped. I managed to answer every question in English.
Aileen
That's fantastic! What did they ask you?
Mai
They asked me to describe a time I solved a problem at work, so I talked about Bridge. The interviewer said she enjoyed hearing about it.
Aileen
Perfect example. Did anything go wrong?
Mai
Well, at one point I couldn't stop saying "um." And they wanted me to do a short role-play with a "guest" — I almost forgot to smile!
Aileen
Ha! Everyone gets nervous. So when will you hear back?
Mai
They promised to let me know by the end of the month. I keep checking my email every five minutes!
Aileen
Try to avoid thinking about it too much. Whatever happens, you should be proud of yourself.
Mai
Thanks, Aileen. If I get it, I'll let you know first!
EXPRESSIONS EXPLANATION
I've been dying to hear.
I have really wanted to hear about it.
聞きたくてたまらなかった
better than I expected
Better than I thought it would be.
思っていたよりよかった
at one point
At one moment during a longer event.
途中で一度、ある時点で
hear back
To get a reply or result from someone.
（結果などの）返事をもらう
Whatever happens, ~
It does not matter what the result is; ~ is still true.
結果がどうであれ、何が起きても

Express Yourself — Free Writing
会話のアイデアを英語で書いてみましょう。
You run into a friend you haven't seen for a few months. They ask how life has been. Tell them about the habits you have changed recently — and something you want to try next.
Think about the conversation you would have and write down your ideas.
e.g. I've given up drinking coffee after lunch, and I sleep much better now.
e.g. My doctor told me to walk more, so I've decided to get off the train one stop early.
e.g. I'm hoping to run a 10K race in the spring.
